short_bio: Director of The Hurt Locker, which won her the Oscar for directing, a first for a woman.
biography:
Kathryn Bigelow was born in San Carlos, California, studied painting at the San Francisco Art Institute and film at Columbia University. Her early features were genre films: Near Dark (1987) and Point Break (1991).

She directed Strange Days (1995) and K-19: The Widowmaker (2002). The Hurt Locker (2008), about a US bomb-disposal team in Iraq, won six Oscars, among them Best Picture and Best Director; no woman had won the directing prize before her.

She followed it with Zero Dark Thirty (2012), on the hunt for Osama bin Laden, and Detroit (2017).
